title: Finite projective summands inherit Tor independence
statement: Let R be a commutative ring and let A and B be commutative R-algebras. For R-modules M,N, write Tor_i^R(M,N) for the i-th homology module of a projective-resolution tensor complex (i.e. the usual Tor groups [def-weil-pbc-tor-modules]). Assume Tor_i^R(A,B)=0 for every i>0. If P is an A-module that is a direct summand of A^m for some finite m (a finite projective A-module), then Tor_i^R(P,B)=0 for every i>0.

source.place: Tag 08IB, lemma-compare-base-change: Tor-independent comparison of derived tensors

proof.text: Fix i > 0. Regard Tor_i^R(-,B) as the left-derived functor F of tensoring on the right with B [def-weil-pbc-tor-modules]. The projective-resolution functor is additive: the chosen lift of a+b is homotopic to the sum of the chosen lifts of a and b, by ProjectiveResolution.liftHomotopy. Composing it with the additive mapHomotopyCategory and homology functors makes F additive.

For j in Fin m, restrict to R the A-linear maps f_j = proj_j composed with s and g_j = r composed with single_j. The sum of f_j followed by g_j is the identity on P: evaluated on x, the sum is r(sum_j single_j(s(x)_j)) = r(s(x)) = x by hsplit. This calculation also applies when m=0, with the empty sum.

By additivity and functoriality [def-weil-pbc-tor-modules], id_{F(P)} is the sum of F(f_j) followed by F(g_j). Each F(f_j) has target F(A), which is zero by hTor i, so every summand is zero. The identity on F(P) is zero, hence F(P) is a zero object. Since i>0 was arbitrary this proves the assertion.
